name: Talkiatry
one_liner: Online psychiatry practice: video visits with a psychiatrist for diagnosis and medication, billed in-network to commercial insurance and Medicare.
best_for: Adults and children 5+ with commercial insurance or Medicare who need a psychiatrist for medication
People who can't find a local psychiatrist with openings
People who want therapy and medication from the same practice (therapy needs a Talkiatry psychiatrist's referral)
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who only want talk therapy without a psychiatrist
People seeking treatment for schizophrenia, primary eating disorders or medication for opioid use disorder (not offered)
short_description: Video psychiatry with Talkiatry's own psychiatrists, in-network with many commercial plans and Medicare; not Medicaid.
long_description: Talkiatry is a US telepsychiatry practice. You complete an online assessment, are matched with a psychiatrist, and have a video evaluation followed by medication-management visits; therapy is available only after referral by a Talkiatry psychiatrist. It treats people aged 5 and up and works mainly through insurance: it is in-network with many commercial plans and Medicare and does not take Medicaid. Its insurance page says it now offers self-pay for people whose insurer it doesn't accept (not for Medicaid or Medicare), but a help-center article still says there is no self-pay option, and no self-pay price is published. Whether controlled medications can be prescribed depends on your state's in-person rules. Its published research is two company-funded retrospective analyses of its own patients (2023 and 2025), with no control group, reporting reduced depression and anxiety scores during treatment.
patient_summary: You fill in an online assessment, get matched with a psychiatrist, and meet by video for an evaluation and then medication follow-ups. You pay your insurance copay or deductible; Medicaid isn't accepted, and self-pay is only offered to some people without a published price.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; self-pay price not published
pricing.notes: In-network with many commercial plans and Medicare; not Medicaid. Talkiatry's insurance page says self-pay is now offered when your insurer isn't accepted (not for Medicaid or Medicare patients), while a help-center article says there is no self-pay option; no self-pay rate is published. Your cost depends on your plan's copay and deductible.

privacy.notes: Talkiatry's California notice says it treats advertising and analytics cookies as a 'sale' and lists identifiers sold in the past year; you can opt out. Your medical records are protected health information under its HIPAA notice, and deletion requests are honored within HIPAA's limits.

seo.title: Talkiatry: Online Psychiatry with Insurance | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Talkiatry offers online psychiatry with licensed psychiatrists. Accepts most insurance. Medication management via video. Book your appointment today.

faqs.a: Talkiatry accepts most major insurance plans including Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and many others. Check their website with your specific plan to confirm coverage.

Yes, Talkiatry psychiatrists can evaluate and treat ADHD, including prescribing stimulant medications in states where telehealth prescribing is permitted. Some states have restrictions on controlled substance prescribing via telehealth.

faqs.q: Is Talkiatry the same as BetterHelp or Talkspace?
faqs.a: No. Talkiatry is psychiatry (medical doctors who can prescribe medication), while BetterHelp and Talkspace primarily offer therapy with licensed therapists. If you need medication, Talkiatry is appropriate. If you need talk therapy without medication, consider therapy platforms.

faqs.q: How quickly can I get an appointment with Talkiatry?
faqs.a: Most patients can get an initial appointment within 1-2 weeks, which is faster than many in-person psychiatrists. Availability varies by location and time of year.
